page: Running Hono on Fastly Compute edge computing platform on Fastly's global network. Fastly CLI installed automatically with template. Setup: npm create hono@latest my-app, select fastly template. Install: npm i. Hello World: Hono app with fire(app) from @fastly/hono-fastly-compute. Use Hono from 'hono' not 'hono/quick' with fire. Run: npm run start, access http://localhost:7676. Deploy: npm run deploy (creates service first time, requires Fastly account). Bindings: KV Stores, Config Stores, Secret Stores, Backends, ACLs, Named Log Streams, Environment Variables. Use buildFire() instead of fire() for typed bindings. Access via c.env. Pass fire.Bindings to Hono<{ Bindings }> generics. Questions: How do I set up Hono on Fastly? How do I deploy? How do I use bindings? What's the difference between fire and buildFire?

sections.manifest: Setup for Fastly Compute. Create project: npm create hono@latest my-app, select fastly template (yarn, pnpm, bun, deno variants). Install dependencies: npm i. Fastly CLI: installed automatically with template. Questions: How do I create project? Which template? What's Fastly CLI?

Hello World on Fastly. File: src/index.ts. Imports: Hono from 'hono', fire from '@fastly/hono-fastly-compute'. Code: new Hono(), app.get('/', (c) => c.text('Hello Fastly!')), fire(app). Note: use 'hono' not 'hono/quick' with fire (fire builds router during initialization). Questions: What's the basic setup? Why 'hono' not 'hono/quick'? What does fire() do?
Development server. Command: npm run start, yarn start, pnpm run start, bun run start. Access: http://localhost:7676. Local development ready. Questions: How do I run locally? What's the port?

Deployment to Fastly. Deploy: npm run deploy, yarn deploy, pnpm run deploy, bun run deploy. First deployment: prompted to create service. Requirements: Fastly account (signup at fastly.com). Questions: How do I deploy? What's required? How do I create account?

Fastly Compute Bindings for platform resources. Resources: KV Stores, Config Stores, Secret Stores, Backends, Access Control Lists, Named Log Streams, Environment Variables. Usage: import buildFire instead of fire. Define bindings: buildFire({ siteData: 'KVStore:site-data' }). Type Hono: new Hono<{ Bindings: typeof fire.Bindings }>. Access via c.env: c.env.siteData.put(key, value). fire.Bindings provides type definitions. Call: fire(app) after setup. Example: KV Store upload operation. Questions: What bindings are available? How do I define bindings? How do I type them? How do I access bindings?
